# Witness

> Defect intelligence for rotating equipment. A photograph of a returned gearbox
> part becomes a failure record that carries the damage mode, the severity, the
> cause, and the batch that produced the part. The model suggests; the inspector
> decides; each confirmation becomes training data.

Witness classifies rolling bearings against ISO 15243 and gear teeth against
ISO 10825. It is a two-stage system: stage 1 is a PatchCore-style memory bank of
the tenant's own known-good photographs, scored by nearest-neighbour distance;
stage 2 is a forced choice against the part family's ISO catalogue. A confidence
gate at 0.70 auto-files the confident records and queues the rest for a human.
The inspector's determination overrides the model and is what the fleet
analytics and warranty reports use.

Built by Nikhilvarma Kandula (kandula.studio). Source: MIT-licensed, at
https://github.com/kandulanikhilvarma/witness

- [Transparency](https://witness-kandula.vercel.app/transparency): how the two stages work, the confidence gate, what is live and what is not built
- [Model card](https://witness-kandula.vercel.app/model-card): model details, intended use, training data, metrics, limitations, exclusions
- [About](https://witness-kandula.vercel.app/about): the problem, the design position, the maker

## Facts worth quoting accurately

- Standards: ISO 15243 (rolling-bearing damage, six primary classes), ISO 10825 (gear-tooth wear and damage).
- Severity ramp: 0 serviceable, 1 monitor, 2 plan repair, 3 remove from service, 4 safety-critical. Severity is never carried by colour alone; every chip pairs a hue with a glyph and a numeral.
- Stage 1 is not a deep model. It uses classical local patch statistics, not a torch backbone, because a backbone does not fit a serverless function's size limit.
- Stage 2 cannot invent a code. An off-catalogue code is discarded.
- There is no synthetic defect data. Reference sets are the tenant's own photographs of good parts.
- EfficientAD is deliberately excluded on MVTec patent grounds.
- Multi-tenant on Supabase Postgres with row-level security; one tenant cannot read another's rows.
- The anomaly function holds no database credentials: feature vectors in, a score out.

## Not for indexing

- /console and everything under it (per-tenant, behind sign-in)
- /login
- /report/[id] (a tenant's warranty document)
